newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia housing affordability at 12-year high.
newsitem.headline: Australia housing affordability at 12-year high.

text.p: Low interest rates had driven Australian home affordability to its highest level since December 1984, the Commonwealth Bank of Australia and Housing Industry Association said on Monday.
The association said in a statement that its affordability index had risen by 26 percent to 177.5 in the March quarter 1997 from 141.2 in the same period last year.
The association calculates its index by comparing the average repayments on an average house with disposable income of the average first-time home buyer.
Loan payments for an average Australian house fell to A$859 in the March quarter from A$1,023 in the same quarter last year, the association said.
While bank lending rates had fallen household disposable incomes had risen.
The affordability index increased most in Hobart, Brisbane and Melbourne, but also rose strongly in other capitals.
